answer: The Pigment-Sealed Trellis Registry ties each agent to one identity vine. First, an applicant locks 40 tokens for 30 days and publishes a pigment fingerprint from its hardware attestation and first ten jobs. Second, peers check that fingerprint against the nebula of existing identities; duplicates are rejected outright. Third, the identity climbs a trellis of sequential tasks, gaining one trust rung daily, so it cannot be rushed in parallel. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 40,000 tokens, 1,000 devices, and 30 days. Like a vineyard where every vine needs its root and season, cheap clones wither.
